result:
All 6 tests pass. 

## Cause

Sessions never expired because of a fail-open chain across four files — no single line was the whole bug:

1. **`src/db/schema.sql:2`** — the `sessions` table had only `id` and `created_at`. No `expires_at` column existed to hold an expiry, and no `user_id` either, even though `createSession` was already inserting one.
2. **`src/lib/session.ts:14`** — `createSession` inserted only `(id, user_id)` and returned `expiresAt: null`. The `defaultExpiry()` helper right below it was written but never called by anything.
3. **`src/lib/session.ts:22`** — `isExpired` returned `false` when `expiresAt` was falsy. So a session with no expiry was treated as *valid forever*, which is exactly the state every session was in.
4. **`src/middleware/auth.ts:10`** — `requireAuth` passed the raw DB row straight to `isExpired`. Rows are snake_case (`expires_at`), `Session` is camelCase (`expiresAt`), so `s.expiresAt` read `undefined` and hit the same fail-open branch. This one mattered independently: fixing only 1–3 would still have left auth passing an unmapped row and never expiring anything.

## Fix

- **`schema.sql`** — `sessions` now has `user_id uuid not null references users(id)` and `expires_at timestamptz not null`.
- **`session.ts`** — `createSession` calls `defaultExpiry()` (1 day, via the `src/lib/time.ts` helpers per the time convention), writes `expires_at`, and returns it. Added `toSession(row)` + a `SessionRow` type to do the snake_case→camelCase mapping in one place.
- **`session.ts`** — `isExpired` now fails **closed**: no expiry means expired, so a missing or unreadable `expires_at` can never grant an unlimited session again.
- **`auth.ts`** — maps the row through `toSession` before the expiry check, and returns the typed `Session`. No caller used the old return value (all 8 API modules just `await requireAuth(req)`), so the type change is safe.
- **`src/lib/__tests__/session.test.ts`** — new, per the vitest/`__tests__` convention. Covers expiry population, all three `isExpired` branches including the fail-closed one, and both `toSession` mappings.

One thing to flag before this ships: `expires_at` is declared `not null`, but any rows already in a live `sessions` table have no value for it. A real deployment needs a migration that backfills existing rows (or adds the column nullable, backfills, then adds the constraint) — this repo has no migrations directory, so I amended the `CREATE TABLE` only. Related: the now-fail-closed `isExpired` means any session predating the fix will be rejected, so expect existing sessions to be logged out on deploy.
